answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: each agent stakes a small bond and builds a verifiable record of useful work before earning full rewards. A newcomer cannot simply wander in and clone itself a hundred times to drain the pool, since every clone must pay separately and prove itself. Good reputation becomes an oasis among cheap identities: scarce, earned slowly, and easy to check. At the zenith of trust, consistent long-lived agents carry more weight, while fresh identities stay limited until proven.
